provenance.pins: datasheet p.1 SOT-23 package drawing: 1 G, 2 S, 3 D

designVerdict: SELECTED as Q1,Q2 - the two FAULT interlocks, one per channel. No longer the PD follower: Q3 is now an MMBT5551 (C7420357), because a 1.6 V worst-case V_GS is too large an offset for the HUSB238A undervoltage detector below a 20 V contract.
notes: NOT THE PD FOLLOWER. Hynetek's Figure 6 'Voltage Regulator' is a BSS138 source follower in the vendor's reference, and this record once described that role. It is C7420357's: see that record for the topology and the vSafe5V margins, and C24833806 for why VDD is tied to 3V3.

ROLE EXPANDED: also fitted as the FAULT interlock transistors, replacing 2N7002 there. V_GS(th) 1.6 V max (this LCSC part, not the 1.5 V of other vendors) against the 2N7002's 2.5 V means the HUSB238A's 2.64 V V_OH leaves 1.04 V of worst-case overdrive rather than 0.14 V. Same part, same footprint, one fewer line on the BOM.

WHY IT LOST THE FOLLOWER ROLE: the detector compares the VBUS pin against a percentage of the requested voltage, so the pass condition is V_GS <= 0.09*V in the 86% band. 1.6 V needs V >= 17.8 V, which fails 9 V, 12 V and 15 V. It remains correct as a logic-level interlock switch, where the threshold being high is irrelevant - the GPIO drives it at 3.3 V.
